column5: The packaged real-control journey owns this test harness.
Process-group behavior uses bounded process integration evidence.
Platform lock behavior uses its dedicated process scenario.
Provider integration scenarios exercise the real CLI process boundary.

column6: A policy change keeps local feedback focused and hosted evidence complete.
Documentation and executable contracts stay synchronized.
A user creates a managed provider session.
A live session remains available after the app exits.
A user recovers the exact owned session after interruption.
A user stops only the selected owned session.
A user deletes one completed session without affecting another session.
A protected session acquires both required power protections.
Low battery removes unsafe protection and reports the reason.
The helper accepts only an authorized bounded lease.
A protected session continues on supervised supported hardware with the lid closed.
A user sees fresh typed session health on the dashboard.
A user selects a session and sees its details.
A user sees useful empty-state guidance.
A user sees an actionable failure without parsed terminal claims.
Background status checks do not steal keyboard focus.
A user opens the new-session form and cannot launch without a project.
A new user completes the first-run setup.
Onboarding detects an authenticated supported provider.
Onboarding explains and observes required macOS approvals.
A user changes a setting and observes the persisted result.
A user receives a typed update state.
A valid update preserves the arm64 and signature contract.
A user receives a typed actionable doctor report.
A user installs one immutable self-contained payload.
Repair restores the exact immutable payload.
Uninstall removes only Detach-owned data selected by the user.
Publication exposes only verified allowlisted artifacts.

column4: Typed state is the only shared state mutation boundary.
Session operations prove the exact run token and process ownership.
Restores validate path, symlink, identity, and JSONL data before replacement.
Power protection owns a user IOKit assertion.
Helper authorization binds audit token, console user, signing, and deadline.
The root helper lease is bounded and ownership safe.
The helper accepts only the typed power protocol.
The power command reports and enforces typed protection state.
Platform power operations preserve the helper safety boundary.
Health claims use typed fresh state.
The app presents typed health state without parsing terminal text.
Session transitions preserve exact process identity.
Session tips remain deterministic and user visible.
Doctor output derives from typed runtime state.
Onboarding leads a new user through supported provider and approval setup.
Settings changes persist and affect only their declared behavior.
Update state and application preserve the signed arm64 contract.
Install, repair, and uninstall mutate only Detach-owned payloads and selected state.
Publication exposes only independently verified allowlisted artifacts.
